q: What is a style sheet language?
options: A language that defines the structure and content of a document
A computer language used to describe the presentation of structured documents
A language that translates source code into machine code
A format for exchanging data between systems
explanation: Style sheet languages describe how content is rendered on screens, printers, or speech synthesizers. Defining structure and content is the job of markup languages like HTML.

q: What is CSS?
options: Cascading Style Sheets, the predominant style sheet language on the web
Computer Style Syntax, a markup language for documents
Coded Structure Standard, a data interchange format
Common Script System, a programming language for browsers
explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It applies colors, fonts, spacing, and layouts to HTML documents.

q: In CSS, what is a selector?
options: The value given to a property
A property and value pair ending with a semicolon
The part of a rule that identifies which HTML elements the styles apply to
The HTML tag that links a .css file
explanation: A selector picks the elements to style, by type, class, ID, attribute, or position. A property and value pair is a declaration.

q: What is a CSS declaration?
options: A selector together with its curly braces
A comment written between /* and */
An HTML attribute named style
A property and its value, separated by a colon and ending with a semicolon
explanation: In `p { line-height: 1.5; }`, `line-height: 1.5;` is a declaration. The selector plus its declarations is a ruleset.

q: What is a ruleset in CSS?
options: A selector combined with its declarations to form a complete CSS rule
A list of all the HTML tags on a page
A file that stores only color values
A group of HTML attributes on one tag
explanation: The general form is `selector { property: value; }`. The whole thing, selector plus declarations, is the ruleset.

options: CSS rules stored in a separate .css file
A style applied directly to an HTML element using the style attribute
CSS rules written inside a `<style>` tag in the head
A style that is used only when printing

q: What is a CSS preprocessor such as Sass or LESS?
options: A browser feature that tests CSS on many devices
A validator that checks HTML for errors
A program that compresses images for the web
A tool for writing more efficient CSS using variables, nesting, and functions
explanation: Preprocessors add variables, nesting, and functions, then produce normal CSS. Compressing CSS files is a separate performance practice.

q: In the BEM naming convention, what do the letters stand for?
options: Block, Element, Modifier
Border, Element, Margin
Background, Effect, Media
Box, Edge, Model
explanation: BEM means Block, Element, Modifier. It keeps class names consistent, which improves readability and reduces conflicts.

q: Which is the correct general form of a CSS ruleset?
options: `selector ( property = value, )`
`property { selector: value; }`
`selector { property: value; }`
`<selector property='value'>`
explanation: The selector comes first, then curly braces holding declarations written as property, colon, value, semicolon.

q: Which symbols start a class selector and an ID selector?
options: `#` for a class and `.` for an ID
`.` for a class and `#` for an ID
`*` for a class and `@` for an ID
`:` for a class and `;` for an ID
explanation: `.highlight` is a class selector and `#main-header` is an ID selector. Swapping the two symbols is a common mistake.

q: Which tag links an external stylesheet, and where does it go?
options: `<style>` inside `<body>`
`<link>` inside `<body>`
`<css>` inside `<head>`
`<link>` inside `<head>`
explanation: External CSS is linked with `<link rel='stylesheet' href='styles.css'>` inside the `<head>` section. `<style>` is for internal stylesheets.

q: Which CSS version added positioning, z-index, and media types?
options: CSS3 (2011 to present)
explanation: CSS2 added these advanced features. CSS1 covered fonts, colors, and text; CSS2.1 corrected CSS2; CSS3 brought modularization.

q: Who proposed Cascading Style Sheets?
options: Tim Berners-Lee and Robert Cailliau
Håkon Wium Lie and Bert Bos
Brendan Eich and Marc Andreessen
Guido van Rossum and James Gosling
explanation: Håkon Wium Lie and Bert Bos proposed CSS. Tim Berners-Lee introduced HTML, which is a markup language.

q: Which list puts the CSS versions in order from oldest to newest?
options: CSS1, CSS2, CSS2.1, CSS3
CSS1, CSS2.1, CSS2, CSS3
CSS2, CSS1, CSS3, CSS2.1
CSS1, CSS3, CSS2, CSS2.1
explanation: CSS1 (1996), CSS2 (1998), CSS2.1 (2011), then CSS3 (2011 to present). CSS2.1 refined CSS2, so it came after it.

q: What is the correct order of the parts inside one CSS declaration?
options: Value, colon, property, semicolon
Property, semicolon, value, colon
Property, colon, value, semicolon
Colon, property, value, semicolon
explanation: A declaration is written `property: value;`, as in `color: blue;`.

q: What is the correct order of steps to style several pages with one external stylesheet?
options: Add a style attribute to every tag, then create a .css file
Create a .css file with the rules, then add a `<link>` tag to it inside the `<head>` of each page
Put a `<link>` tag inside `<body>`, then write the rules inside the HTML
Write the rules in a `<style>` tag, then remove the `<head>` section
explanation: Write the rules once in a .css file, then link that file from each page's `<head>`. Later changes are made only in the .css file.

q: Which describes how web styling developed over time?
options: CSS3 first, then HTML styling attributes, then CSS1
CSS2 first, then HTML styling attributes, then CSS1
Preprocessors first, then CSS1, then HTML styling attributes
Styling with HTML attributes like font, color, and bgcolor, then CSS proposed, then CSS3 modules
explanation: Early pages were styled with HTML attributes, which became unwieldy. CSS was proposed to separate content from presentation, and CSS3 later split it into modules.

q: Which is NOT one of the lesson's best practices in CSS?
options: Use external stylesheets
Use inline styles on every element so each tag can be updated easily
Test across browsers
Adopt naming conventions such as BEM
explanation: Inline styles are discouraged because of poor separation of concerns and maintainability issues. The other three are listed best practices.

q: Which pairing of a CSS version and its feature is mismatched?
options: CSS1: fonts, colors, and text attributes
CSS2: positioning and z-index
CSS2.1: refined CSS2 and corrected errors
CSS3: introduced basic font styling for the first time
explanation: Basic font styling came with CSS1. CSS3 introduced modularization, with features like transitions, animations, and flexbox.

q: Which statement about selectors is NOT true?
options: A type selector selects elements by their tag name
An ID selector is meant to select many elements that share one name
A class selector selects elements by their class attribute
An attribute selector selects elements based on attributes and attribute values
explanation: An ID selector selects a unique element. Many elements sharing a name is what a class is for.

q: Which is NOT an application of CSS in the lesson?
options: Performing calculations on user data
Responsive designs for desktops, tablets, and smartphones
High-contrast modes or larger fonts for accessibility
Print styles that target the print media type
explanation: CSS controls presentation. Calculations and logic are done by programming languages such as JavaScript.

A `

` element has class 'special' and id 'unique'. What color is its text?
options: Black
Blue
Red
Purple, a mix of all three
explanation: All three rules match, but they conflict. The ID selector has the highest specificity, so `#unique` wins and the text is red.

q: A student writes this CSS. The font size is never applied. What is the error?
options: `h1` must be written as `.h1`
`24px` must be written without the px
The curly braces should be parentheses
The semicolon after `blue` is missing, so the two declarations run together
explanation: Each declaration must end with a semicolon. The fix is `color: blue;` followed by `font-size: 24px;`.

q: A student writes this. The paragraph is not highlighted. What is the error?
options: `.highlight` selects class='highlight', but the paragraph uses id='highlight'
`background-color` is not a CSS property
`yellow` is not a valid color value
Paragraphs cannot have a background color
explanation: A dot selects a class. Either change the HTML to `class='highlight'` or change the selector to `#highlight`.

q: A 40-page website must share one look and be easy to update. Which way of applying CSS fits best?
options: Inline styles on every element
An internal `<style>` tag copied into every page
One external .css file linked from each page with `<link>`
HTML attributes like font and bgcolor
explanation: External stylesheets are recommended for larger websites: one change in the .css file updates all 40 pages. Copies or inline styles must be edited page by page.

q: A one-page event invitation needs its styles kept inside the same HTML file. Which method does the lesson suggest?
options: An external stylesheet
An internal stylesheet in a `<style>` tag inside `<head>`
An inline style attribute on every tag
A Sass file
explanation: Internal stylesheets suit single-page websites or page-level styles. External files are for larger sites, and inline styles are discouraged.

q: How many rulesets and how many declarations are in this CSS?
options: 2 rulesets and 3 declarations
1 ruleset and 3 declarations
2 rulesets and 4 declarations
3 rulesets and 3 declarations
explanation: There are two selectors, `p` and `.special`, so 2 rulesets. `p` has 2 declarations and `.special` has 1, so 2 + 1 = 3.

q: Which rule sets a font size of 24px on only the element with id 'main-header'?
options: `.main-header { font-size: 24px; }`
`main-header { font-size: 24px; }`
`#main-header { font-size: 24px; }`
`#main-header { font-size = 24px }`
explanation: An ID selector starts with `#`, and a declaration uses a colon and a semicolon. `.main-header` would select a class, and `=` is not CSS syntax.

q: What color is the text of this paragraph?
options: Black
Green
Default browser color
Orange
explanation: The type rule says black and the class rule says green, but the inline style attribute is the most specific of all, so the text is orange.

q: All paragraphs should be gray, and any element with class 'warning' should be red. Which CSS does this?
options: `p { color: gray; } .warning { color: red; }`
`p { color: gray; } #warning { color: red; }`
`.p { color: gray; } .warning { color: red; }`
`p { color: gray; } warning { color: red; }`
explanation: `p` is a type selector for all paragraphs, and `.warning` is a class selector. `#warning` would need an id, `.p` needs class='p', and `warning` looks for a tag named warning.
